newsitem.title: SPAIN: BoS may be in market to strengthen peseta - dealers.
newsitem.headline: BoS may be in market to strengthen peseta - dealers.

text.p: Rumours of Bank of Spain's intervention were keeping the peseta glued to 84.70 versus the mark at midday, dealers said on Thursday.
They were suggesting the Bank of Spain could have sold mark and bought pesetas in order to strengthen the weak Spanish currency.
"I have the feeling that the Bank of Spain is in the market, but we are not sure," a dealer said.
The Bank of Spain did not, as is its practice, comment on these rumours.
At around 1320 GMT the peseta was trading at 84.67/70 versus the mark after 84.68/71 at the opening this morning and a yesterday's closing level of 84.62/65.
